quotes_used_verbatim: U.S. citizens on closed-loop cruises (cruises that begin and end at the same U.S. port) are able to enter the United States with a birth certificate and government-issued photo ID.
Please be aware that you may still be required to present a passport to enter the countries your cruise ship is visiting.
primary_sources.definition_verified: Closed-loop cruise = departs from and returns to the same U.S. port.

primary_sources.source: U.S. State Department cruise-ship passenger guidance
primary_sources.how_obtained: Direct fetch of the travel.state.gov cruise-ship-passengers page returned HTTP 403; content was obtained via domain-restricted search of travel.state.gov and cbp.gov. Recorded here because the retrieval route is weaker than a direct fetch and a reader should know that.
primary_sources.substance_used: Recommendation to travel with a passport BOOK even when the cruise line does not require it, because a passport book is needed to fly home internationally in an emergency; named scenarios include unexpected medical evacuation, the ship docking at a different port, and ship damage or mechanical problems requiring passengers to go ashore where a passport is required; plus the advice to make colour copies of the photo page and leave one with someone at home.
primary_sources.paraphrase_note: State Department material is paraphrased rather than quoted verbatim, because it was not obtained by direct page fetch.

claims.not_claimed: NO per-country passport validity rule, NO blank-page requirement figure, NO specific requirement for minors or for adults travelling with a child who is not theirs, and NO notarised-letter requirement is asserted. The article explicitly routes those to the cruise line in writing and to current official guidance, and states why: they interact, are not uniform, and change.
claims.passport_card: The book-not-card point is presented as following from the State Department recommendation being specifically for a passport book (the book is what permits international air travel). No separate card-policy citation was obtained.
claims.internal_anchor: The propulsion-problem example is our own published Getaway Aug 2026 logbook, linked.
claims.disclaimer_in_body: The article states in its own text that it is travel guidance and not legal advice, is dated, and should be verified against CBP and State before sailing.

voice_audit.scope: full article body (itemprop=articleBody), not the summary
voice_audit.machine_tell_scan: 0 banned cruise-marketing terms, 0 generic AI tells, 0 copulative-avoidance constructions (serves as / stands as / represents a / embodies / marks a / constitutes), 0 translationese terms, 0 inline self-correction leakage, 0 ellipses.
voice_audit.corpus_comparison: em-dash density and sentence-length variance compared against four published InTheWake articles (cruise-tipping-2026, what-cruise-actually-costs-2026, great-stirrup-cay-changes-2026, cruise-pool-lifts-accessibility-gap), whose measured em-dash densities span 7.7-16.0 per 1000 words. This page falls inside that range.
voice_audit.corrections_applied: cruise-passport-or-birth-certificate: 'careful rather than comprehensive' changed to 'careful rather than complete' (one generic-AI-tell hit). No other page required an edit.
voice_audit.honest_limit: This attestation records a mechanical scan plus author judgment. It measures the presence of known tells and structural variance; it cannot certify that the prose reads as lived experience to a human reader.
